extractionLoop.stage1_upfrontSkim: No sum is established by this record, and the figures put to the witness were not adopted by him. What the hearing does record about the plumbing is how the money moved: the IMF payment was "to be made in dollars and deposited in the Russian Central Bank's account at the New York Federal Reserve Bank. Some of the money was then invested in U.S. T-bills, while the remainder was transferred to the Central Bank's U.S. dollar clearing account at the Republic Bank of New York", after which the Central Bank traded in the Russian foreign exchange market "directly with 30 or so large Russian banks".
extractionLoop.stage2_structuralCompromise: The structural feature named by the witness is the "lockup" — the arrangement for "protecting the money so that it remains in a closed circuit within the IMF". A disbursement that never leaves the official circuit cannot be followed into the country it was lent to, and the witness invoked that design as the reason a money-laundering investigation would not bear on the loan.
extractionLoop.stage3_informationFog: The fog here is intra-governmental and the witness describes its mechanics without apology. Somebody in "the upper middle levels of the State Department" learned of a criminal inquiry into the Bank of New York; "That individual and the State Department did exactly what the book requires. They made sure that the Justice Department was aware of this." Then the procedure took over: "the Justice Department will then brief the State Department at an appropriate level when the facts and the case are developed to the point where they are felt to have some kind of foreign policy relevance. And that happened in August, and I was part of that briefing." The dates are the point: "we, the Department, originally found out about the Bank of New York case in the spring", and the briefing to the Deputy Secretary came in August. The July loan sits between them.
extractionLoop.stage4_monopolyWindfall: Not established by this record, and the dossier claims none. No money is traced to any person in the pages read, and no beneficiary is named.
extractionLoop.stage5_merseyWhitewash: The containment is in the witness's own assessment and in the reasons he gives for it. Asked whether the administration may have concealed what it knew, Talbott said he believed "the administration—and that means both the State Department and the Treasury Department—handled this very delicate matter absolutely appropriately", citing "a very important principle operating in our Government, which is the sanctity of the grand jury process" under which "all officials who know about it are very constrained in what they can do about it." On whether the knowledge should have affected the loan, he deferred: "you would have to ask Treasury. Secretary Summers did address this case in some detail earlier in the week, but my impression is that it would not have had any effect on that."

closedLoopRatchet.inheritedFramework: IMF disbursement through a borrowing central bank's account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, with a lockup intended to keep the funds in a closed official circuit, and a grand-jury confidentiality rule that constrains what officials who learn of an investigation may do with the knowledge.
closedLoopRatchet.newFrameworkCreated: Nothing in what was read. The witness points instead at a law that did not arrive: "the Duma did pass a money laundering law, and the Yeltsin administration vetoed it. We were critical of that decision."
closedLoopRatchet.closedLoopRecirculation: Not traced by this source. The loop this record can show is a procedural one: a criminal inquiry is learned of, referred to Justice as the rules require, and held there until Justice judges it to have "foreign policy relevance" — by which time the lending decision it might have borne on has been taken.

decoyVsLedger.viralDecoy: That the 1998 IMF bailout of Russia was stolen before it arrived — $3.9 billion of $4.8 billion never entering the country — and that Washington knew the money was being laundered through the Bank of New York and lent anyway.
decoyVsLedger.whyDecoyFails: BOTH HALVES OF THAT APPEAR IN THIS HEARING, AND NEITHER IS A FINDING. The $3.9 billion figure was put to the witness by the committee chairman as "the assertion by the fired Russian Prosecutor General Yuriy Skuratov, reported in the press". Talbott's answer was: "I certainly cannot vouch for that. Both the IMF external auditors, PricewaterhouseCoopers, in particular, the U.S. Government, are all seeking to establish the facts." Pressed again, he said: "I would really prefer to confine myself to what our own authorities have been able to establish." The claim that Rubin and Summers knew before the July loan was likewise a senator reading the New York Times of 8 September 1999 into the record, and the witness did not confirm it — he said "you would have to ask Treasury." So neither number nor name is established here, and this dossier asserts neither. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED IS THE WITNESS'S OWN TIMELINE, given on his own knowledge, and it is enough. The State Department "originally found out about the Bank of New York case in the spring" of 1999. It referred the matter to Justice, as the rules required. Justice briefed the Deputy Secretary of State "in August". The IMF loan went in July. Asked whether that knowledge should have affected the lending decision, the Deputy Secretary of State said "my impression is that it would not have had any effect on that." That is not a conspiracy; it is a design. The procedure places the information where it cannot reach the decision until after the decision, and the official describes the procedure working as intended and calls the handling "absolutely appropriately". The grand-jury principle he cites is a real and legitimate one — which is exactly why the asymmetry it produces is structural rather than corrupt. NO FINDING of any kind is made by this committee in the pages read, and the Bank of New York prosecution itself was not read.
decoyVsLedger.documentedLedger: "Corruption in Russia", hearings before the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations, 106th Congress, 23 and 30 September 1999, S. Hrg. 106-260. The record contains: Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott's testimony that the State Department "originally found out about the Bank of New York case in the spring", that an official at "the upper middle levels" of the Department who learned of the criminal inquiry "made sure that the Justice Department was aware of this", that Justice briefs State "when the facts and the case are developed to the point where they are felt to have some kind of foreign policy relevance", that "that happened in August" and he was part of that briefing, that the loan in the relevant timeframe was the July IMF loan covered by the lockup "protecting the money so that it remains in a closed circuit within the IMF", and that on whether the knowledge should have affected it, "you would have to ask Treasury ... my impression is that it would not have had any effect on that"; his view that the administration "handled this very delicate matter absolutely appropriately", citing "the sanctity of the grand jury process"; his refusal to vouch for or deny the chairman's assertion, sourced to the dismissed Russian Prosecutor General via the press, that $3.9 billion of a $4.8 billion 1998 IMF package never entered Russia, pending PricewaterhouseCoopers as IMF external auditors and US agencies establishing the facts; a description in the record of the disbursement route through the Russian Central Bank's account at the New York Fed, partly into US Treasury bills and partly to a dollar clearing account at Republic Bank of New York, followed by trading directly with some thirty large Russian banks; and the statement that the Duma passed a money laundering law which the Yeltsin administration vetoed, a decision the United States was critical of. Senator Wellstone's quotation of a New York Times report that Treasury Secretary Rubin and Deputy Secretary Summers knew of the investigation before a $640 million July loan installment was approved is recorded as a question, and was not confirmed by the witness.

citations.quoteOrFact: Downloaded from govinfo.gov (344 KB) and read as extracted text. THE CENTRAL EXCHANGE, AND THE CARE IT REQUIRES. Senator Wellstone put to Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott a quotation from the New York Times of 8 September 1999: "The Clinton Administration learned of the Federal investigation into allegations of Russian money laundering at the Bank of New York 5 months earlier than it previously acknowledged, senior Administration officials said today", and "Then Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Deputy Treasury Secretary Larry Summers both knew about the investigation before our Government approved a $640 million installment of loans to Russia in July." THAT IS A SENATOR READING A NEWSPAPER INTO THE RECORD, NOT A FINDING, AND THE WITNESS DID NOT CONFIRM IT. What Talbott did say under questioning, on his own knowledge, is the part this dossier rests on: "It is true that—that what I would call the upper middle levels of the State Department, somebody did find out about the fact that there was a judicial inquiry or a criminal inquiry elsewhere in the United States having to do with the Bank of New York. That individual and the State Department did exactly what the book requires. They made sure that the Justice Department was aware of this. And the procedure here is that the Justice Department will then brief the State Department at an appropriate level when the facts and the case are developed to the point where they are felt to have some kind of foreign policy relevance. And that happened in August, and I was part of that briefing. So the—we originally—we, the Department, originally found out about the Bank of New York case in the spring. It was briefed to me, Ambassador Sestanovich and some others, a few weeks ago in August." ON WHETHER IT SHOULD HAVE AFFECTED THE JULY LOAN, asked twice: "The loan you referred to—the loan that would have been in the timeframe here would have been the loan in July, the IMF loan in July, which is covered by this ... lockup ... That is, protecting the money so that it remains in a closed circuit within the IMF. So I—you would have to ask Treasury. Secretary Summers did address this case in some detail earlier in the week, but my impression is that it would not have had any effect on that." He also said he believed "the administration—and that means both the State Department and the Treasury Department—handled this very delicate matter absolutely appropriately", citing "the sanctity of the grand jury process". ON THE LARGER ALLEGATION, PUT BY THE CHAIRMAN AND NOT CONFIRMED: Senator Helms asked "What do you know about the assertion by the fired Russian Prosecutor General Yuriy Skuratov, reported in the press that $3.9 billion of the $4.8 billion IMF bail-out for Russia in 1998 never entered Russia? Do you deny that?" Talbott: "I certainly cannot vouch for that. Both the IMF external auditors, PricewaterhouseCoopers, in particular, the U.S. Government, are all seeking to establish the facts, and we will rely on the facts as our own agencies establish." Pressed again — "Do you not believe that it was sent by the Russian Central Bank directly to commercial banks, bypassing the currency market, is that not a matter of fact?" — he said: "I would really prefer to confine myself to what our own authorities have been able to establish." SO THE SKURATOV FIGURE IS AN ASSERTION PUT TO A WITNESS WHO DECLINED TO ADOPT OR DENY IT, and it is not asserted here. ON THE MECHANICS, from material in the record: the IMF payment was "to be made in dollars and deposited in the Russian Central Bank's account at the New York Federal Reserve Bank. Some of the money was then invested in U.S. T-bills, while the remainder was transferred to the Central Bank's U.S. dollar clearing account at the Republic Bank of New York", and over July and August the Central Bank traded in the Russian foreign exchange market "directly with 30 or so large Russian banks". ALSO RECORDED: the Duma passed a money laundering law and "the Yeltsin administration vetoed it", which the witness said the United States was "critical of". NO FINDING OF ANY KIND is made by this committee in the pages read, no money is traced to any person, and the Bank of New York prosecution itself was not read.
